name: Hong Kong by Night: Kuei-jin & Eastern Shen (Lore)

text.content:
World of Darkness: Hong Kong (1998) centers overwhelmingly on the Kuei-jin (Cathayan vampires), hengeyokai (shapeshifters), Eastern wraiths of the Dark Kingdom of Jade, and other shen native to Cathay's cosmology of Chi, Yin, and Yang — mechanics this Kindred-focused system does not support. The following pages summarize that material purely as Storyteller-facing antagonist and setting flavor: named Kuei-jin should be run as NPC threats and political forces surrounding the handful of remaining Western Kindred (see the Actors in packs/city-npcs/ prefixed hong-kong-by-night-), never as playable character types.

On July 1, 1997, the British Crown Colony of Hong Kong reverted to the People's Republic of China. For the supernatural community this meant far more than a change of government: it marked the return of the Flame Court, the local Kuei-jin power structure, and the near-total exodus of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}'s Kindred population, which had dominated the territory for over 150 years under the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.OpCOs3PLjmtl0QVu]{Ventrue} Tai-pan Robert Pedder.

pages.name: The Flame Court and the Righteous Devils

text.content:
The Flame Court is the loose confederation of Kuei-jin wu (packs) that claims dominion over Hong Kong. Its long-resident faction, the Righteous Devils, consists of Chinese Kuei-jin who struck an understanding with Tai-pan Pedder decades ago, trading tacit peace for tolerance of the Kin-jin presence. With Pedder gone, the Righteous Devils intend to rule the night openly. They nominally answer to the de facto ancestor Angúo Chun, though most are unbound by any wu loyalty, leaving succession an open and dangerous question.

Angúo Chun spent years using the heimin intermediary Lao Chi to cultivate friendly relations with Pedder, lulling the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} into believing Kuei-jin rule would not disturb Kindred interests — while quietly organizing the Righteous Devils for the eventual overthrow of the "foreign interlopers." He now believes possessing the cursed sword Dragon of the Night (see below) would let him prevent mainland Kuei-jin from usurping his place and eliminate the remaining Kin-jin outright.

Jun Yow leads the mainland-aligned wu Victorious Whirlwind, sent by the Council of Mandarins to reclaim Hong Kong for the Flame Court proper. She commands the reformed chih-mei Bing Kai, a Mongol general and torturer of women in life, and the ex-Red Guard Bao Qun, both serving out harsh atonements (kôa) under her authority. Jun Yow hopes the cursed katana would let her wu overcome Chun and assert direct mainland rulership of the city.

Legend holds that the malevolent bodhisattva known as the Flame-Eater, a prophet-cult-leader who once terrorized pirates in the region, was bound centuries ago by the Scarlet Phoenix Court's wu and now sleeps beneath Hong Kong, feeding on the land's dragons and awaiting the apocalyptic Sixth Age.

Nuan Mei, a hedonistic Kuei-jin who broke with her wu to declare herself heimin (outcast), now spends more time among nature spirits and hengeyokai than her own kind, seeking meaning her mortal life never gave her. She fears what Chinese rule will mean for her shapeshifter friends but is determined to remain in Hong Kong.

Bishamon Kazuko, a Japanese Kuei-jin, has come to Hong Kong specifically hunting the cursed sword Dragon of the Night, seeking to destroy it and lift the curse that has haunted her family's name for generations.

Qian Shi, a Kumo (goblin spider) smuggler, arranged for the katana's illicit arrival in Hong Kong and wants its Chi to bolster his own magic — and, should he learn of its power against shen, to eliminate rivals in the supernatural underworld.

Gan Shuo, an akuma (demon-corrupted Kuei-jin) serving an unnamed dark master, commands an army of animated corpses and desires the sword for his patron's ends.

Ling Chu, a Khan (Kuei-jin "supercop" of the Ministry of Ghosts) investigating a murder committed with the cursed katana, confronts threats to Hong Kong's supernatural order directly and without the patience for shen protocol that other factions observe.

pages.name: Eastern Wraiths: The Dark Kingdom of Jade

text.content:
A gateway (Wall Rating 5) to the Dark Kingdom of Jade sits hidden in a sub-basement of the Bank of China Tower in Central, unknowingly built atop a dragon line of Yin energy by the tower's own designers. The wraiths of Necropolis Hong Kong answer to the Jade Emperor and have been ordered to acquire the cursed katana Dragon of the Night by any means, including influencing living relatives of Hong Kong's mortals to help locate it. A minority of Stygian-aligned wraiths also operate in the territory, dedicated to protecting Westerners who die there, and may attempt to spirit the sword away via the Midnight Express rather than let it fall to the Jade Emperor.

Kowloon Walled City (Wall Rating 6, demolished in the real world in 1993-94 but a notorious supernatural hotspot in this setting) was a lawless no-go zone even for Hong Kong police, ruled by triad gangs, sweatshops, and unlicensed clinics; it remains a significant node for wraith and Kuei-jin activity in Kowloon's underworld.

pages.name: The Cursed Katana: Dragon of the Night

text.content:
The centerpiece artifact of the book's included story ("Dragon of the Night") is Tatsuko Sayo, a katana forged by the master swordsmith Isamu Harujiro in medieval Japan. Isamu tried to cheat the kami who commissioned the blade by substituting false swords for destruction, earning a curse that has followed the weapon and his own spirit for centuries.

The sword grants its wielder bonus Melee skill, extra (aggravated, versus shen) damage, the ability to drain and bestow Chi, passage into the spirit worlds without figurines, and resistance to mind control — but curses the wielder to draw shen blood every time it is unsheathed (or turn it upon themselves) and to be subject to the vengeful, controlling P'o of Isamu Harujiro bound within the hilt. Virtually every faction in Hong Kong's supernatural community — the Righteous Devils, Victorious Whirlwind, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}, the Dark Kingdom of Jade, the Stygians, the Technocracy's Syndicate, rival wizard sects the Wu-Keng and Wu Lung, the mummy Michaela Neff, and the demon hunter Ren Wei — wants to possess, study, or destroy it. This makes the sword a ready-made Storyteller plot hook for any story needing every supernatural power bloc in Hong Kong to converge on a single MacGuffin.
